subject: [PATCH 0/2] crypto: use vmalloc() for large stream workspaces

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: Agreed with Rik's assessment and provided additional Reviewed-by tags for both patches.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 07:07:39AM -0800, Usama Arif wrote:
> The zstd acomp streams retain their workspaces after the last transform
> has been freed. The first is allocated during transform initialization;
> additional per-CPU streams are allocated on demand. They are released
> when the algorithm is unregistered.
> 
> In a 4 KiB-page x86-64 build, each stream requests 1,566,281 bytes.
> If kvmalloc() succeeds via kmalloc(), it occupies an order-9 block
> (2 MiB). vmalloc() needs 383 backing pages (1,532 KiB), 516 KiB fewer
> per stream. Across 384 populated streams, that is 193.5 MiB less
> workspace backing if all would have used kmalloc(). There is no such
> gain when kvmalloc() already falls back to vmalloc().
> 
> Use vmalloc() and vfree() directly to avoid the high-order allocation.
> This uses vmalloc address space, page tables and bookkeeping; the
> figures above compare workspace backing only.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

Nice catch. Given the lifetime of these streams, there really isn't
enough turnover to justify the kmalloc optimization to begin with.

Reviewed-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>

2026-11-12.patch_summary: The patch series aims to optimize memory allocation for large stream workspaces in the crypto subsystem by switching from kmalloc() to vmalloc(). This change is motivated by the observation that kvmalloc() can lead to inefficient high-order allocations, resulting in significant memory usage. The patches replace kmalloc() with vmalloc() for zstd and deflate algorithms, reducing workspace backing size and improving performance.

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary: Pointed out that vmalloc() doesn't avoid high-order allocations and suggested rephrasing the patch description. Provided Reviewed-by and Tested-by tags for both patches.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Usama,

Usama Arif writes:
>Use vmalloc() and vfree() directly to avoid the high-order allocation.

vmalloc() doesn't avoid high-order allocations any more. Since
a06157804399 ("mm/vmalloc: request large order pages from buddy
allocator"), vm_area_alloc_pages() first tries the largest order that
fits, and splits the block up afterwards. So for these 383 pages it still
asks for an order-8 block first, then order 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1.

What the patch does avoid is kmalloc() rounding the 1.5 MiB up to a 2 MiB
block, which is where the 516 KiB per stream comes from. Maybe say that
instead?

Once that's fixed, please feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Chris

reviews.author: Rik van Riel
reviews.summary: Identified the issue of high-order allocations due to kvmalloc() and suggested using vmalloc() instead. Provided Reviewed-by tags for both patches.

reviews.author: Herbert Xu
reviews.summary: Applied the patches after reviewing them.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 07:07:38AM -0800, Usama Arif wrote:
> The zstd and deflate acomp implementations retain per-CPU stream
> workspaces until the algorithms are unregistered. On x86-64 with 4 KiB
> pages, kvmalloc() can back them with order-9 and order-6 kmalloc()
> blocks, respectively.
> 
> Use vmalloc() and vfree() instead. For a server with 384 CPUs, if
> we have streams on all of the CPUs and kvmalloc() takes the
> kmalloc() path for every stream, their workspaces use 193.5 MiB more
> for zstd and 42 MiB for deflate.
> 
> In five before/after boot pairs on a 96-vCPU x86-64 VM with 8 GiB RAM,
> the test populated both algorithms crypto workspaces on every CPU. All
> 192 baseline workspaces used kmalloc() without these patches. The patches
> reduced workspace backing by 48.375 MiB for zstd and 10.5 MiB for deflate
> \u201458.875 MiB combined\u2014in each pair.
> 
> In five before/after runs in a 4-vCPU x86-64 VM, median compression
> and decompression throughput changed by less than 1% (-0.93% to +0.64%).
> Inputs were 4 KiB and 64 KiB synthetic buffers containing pseudorandom
> data or a 50/50 mix of repeating-pattern and pseudorandom bytes.
> The differences were within the observed run-to-run variation.
>  
> Usama Arif (2):
>   crypto: zstd - use vmalloc() for stream workspaces
>   crypto: deflate - use vmalloc() for stream workspaces
> 
>  crypto/deflate.c | 5 +++--
>  crypto/zstd.c    | 4 ++--
>  2 files changed, 5 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
> 
> -- 
> 2.53.0-Meta

All applied.  Thanks.
--
